name: por-output-chain-deglitch
description: Deglitch dwell, qualifying-brownout-dip capture and chatter rejection of design/por_output_chain.sch, at nominal and half IBIAS, over the full 81-point PVT grid. Since #200 the grid also carries the filter's glitch-rejection WIDTH margin: a third chatter burst at 1.05 us (5 % wider than the 1 us the checks above use), with the one-shot's own charge loss recorded as tim_loss_wide_pct and tim_loss_1us_pct. Those two are deliberately limit-free -- they are the margin, and a bound on them would only ever report a flip, not the movement that precedes it.
claim: spec/target-spec.md#por-brownout -- fills that row's open TBD by publishing the deglitch dwell time this cell designs to, and shows it stays under the row's T_dip,min = 10 us so a qualifying dip re-asserts RESETn and regenerates the full spec/target-spec.md#por-reset-pulse. Also covers the no-early/no-double-pulse edge case: sub-dwell POR_RAW chatter, applied both during assertion and after release, changes nothing at the pin. Deglitch is this cell's time-domain mechanism per DR-005 and is separate from the comparator's static hysteresis (#10). Deterministic corners only -- the full brownout sweep is #14's job.

dwell_pgdg_halfib_us.description: THE por-brownout check: the deglitch dwell must stay under the row's T_dip,min = 10 us, measured at the filter output on the stress DUT (half nominal IBIAS -- less bias current means a slower filter). Expected to bind at ss/-40c

dwell_pgdg_1x_us.description: same dwell at the DR-005 nominal 0.5 uA IBIAS -- the number published against the spec row's TBD

reassert_validlow_us.description: end-to-end: POR_RAW falling to RESETn at a valid logic low (0.3 V) at the pin, including the release NAND and the output driver. This is what a downstream digital domain actually sees

resetn_min_during_dip.description: the qualifying 10 us dip really does re-assert RESETn to a valid low -- not a partial droop. A dwell that crept over 10 us at some corner fails here even if the crossing measurement above found something

resetn_max_after_dip.description: no double pulse: after the dip the FULL pulse regenerates, so RESETn stays asserted to the end of the run (the shortest pulse anywhere on the grid is >4 ms; this window is 0.5 ms)

pgdg_min_during_chatter.description: three 1 us sub-dwell glitches on POR_RAW do not move the filter output at all -- this is the deglitch doing its job, measured where it happens

resetn_max_during_chatter.description: no early release: chatter while the pulse is still running never lets RESETn go high

pgdg_min_during_wide_chatter.description: #200's width-margin check. Three 1.05 us glitches -- 5 % wider than the 1 us burst above -- applied after the qualifying dip has restarted the pulse, still leave the filter output near the rail. 1.05 us is inside the bracket control/width_results.md measures the rejection ceiling in at the two fastest corners (post-layout: rejected at 1.0 us, disturbed at 1.25 us; schematic: 1.75 / 2.0 us), so it is a wider width the design AS DRAWN still passes at every corner rather than a width picked for comfort. The 2.0 V bound sits below the worst point this manifest produces -- 2.45 V post-layout at ff/125 C/2.97 V, 2.93 V schematic -- and well above the 1.27 V a glitch that actually propagates leaves behind (width_results.md, post-layout ff/125 C/3.63 V at 1.25 us)

tim_min_during_wide_chatter_v.description: the functional half of #200's width-margin check, and the half with the teeth: across the wider burst the one-shot's timer node keeps its charge. A glitch that propagates fires XMDIS and slams TIM to within tens of mV of VSS -- the CDG = 98 fF failure design/por_output_chain.md records -- and that, not PGDG drooping, is the functional failure (it is also the quantity control/width_results.md's rejected/partial/through verdict is defined on). Undisturbed, TIM sits at 0.39-0.58 V here across the grid, so 0.25 V separates 'kept its charge' from 'restarted' with margin at every corner. It is deliberately NOT a bound on the margin itself: the margin is tim_loss_wide_pct, which carries no limit so that a re-run reports it moving rather than only flipping

resetn_min_after_release.description: no spurious re-assertion: the same chatter applied after release never pulls RESETn down

tpulse_after_chatter_ms.description: the pulse is neither truncated nor restarted by the chatter. The upper bound is the discriminator: a glitch that got through would have reset the timer at 1.2 ms and pushed the release ~0.9 ms later than the un-chattered pulse recorded in sim/por-output-chain-pulse/

iq_asserted_1x_na.description: reset-asserted draw before POR_RAW goes high; third independent measurement of this cell's por-iq share
